What it does: Gets computer system info from CIM/WMI (for example machine name and total RAM) and stores it in $c.
Risk: Low. Could fail if CIM/WMI service has issues or permissions are restricted.

What it does: Gets free space on C: drive and stores just the Free value in $d.
Gets all running processes, sorts by working set memory (largest first), keeps top 5, stores in $p.
Risk: Low to Medium. On very busy systems, process enumeration/sorting can be a little heavy.

What it does: Reads latest 10 events from System log, filters to error level (Level 2), stores in $e.
Reads or changes system parameter?: Reads event log information only (no change).
Risk: Medium. Event messages can contain sensitive details; access may be denied for low-privileged users.

What it does: Starts query for user profiles and begins a filter block for stale profiles, storing results in $u.
Reads or changes system parameter?: Reads user profile metadata only (no change).
Risk: Low to Medium. Can reveal user/profile inventory details.

What it does: Completes filter: keeps non-special profiles not used in last 90 days.
Risk: Low to Medium. Same privacy/inventory exposure concern; no destructive action.

What it does: Prints computer name and total physical memory from $c to console.
Reads or changes system parameter?: No system change; writes output only.
Risk: Low. Could expose host details if output is shared.

What it does: Converts free bytes in $d to GB (rounded to 2 decimals) and prints result.
Reads or changes system parameter?: No system change; writes output only.

What it does: Loops through top 5 processes in $p and prints process name and memory usage.
Reads or changes system parameter?: No system change; writes output only.
Risk: Low. Could expose running process names and memory usage.

What it does: Loops through filtered events in $e and prints event time and message text.
Reads or changes system parameter?: No system change; writes output only.
Risk: Medium. Event messages can include sensitive operational details.

What it does: If stale profile count is greater than zero, prints a summary count.
Reads or changes system parameter?: Reads variable data only; no system change.
